newsitem.title: JAPAN: Indian official says foreign investment improving.
newsitem.headline: Indian official says foreign investment improving.

text.p: India's Finance Secretary Montek Singh Ahluwalia said on Thursday he expected foreign investment in India to improve during the rest of 1996.
Portfolio investment in India's stock market by foreign institutional investors fell in August after strong growth in April, May and June, he said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.

"I would not conclude from August figures that there is a slowing down in foreign investment. We are continuing growth. I expect in the course of the rest of the year even the foreign institutional investor inflow will improve," he said.
The finance secretary said it would take India a couple of years to bring economic growth to a stable level.
He said he expects economic growth of about 6.6 percent in the current fiscal year to March 31, 1997, after growth of seven percent in the previous year.

He said: "We would not call it a slowdown. Last year's growth was a peak reflecting a top of the recovery. We are now getting on to more steady growth. But our intention is to stabilise at around seven percent. It may take a year or two to get to a stable level of growth in India."
